about: Shetach territories and heads over time, the United States first (the owner's idea, Nov 6; started Nov 8). It holds what a map of any year needs: whose shetach each area was in, and who headed each shetach. 'areas' is keyed by the map's piece id, '<state>:<shetach id>' as in web/data/centers.geojson ('US-OR:oregon' is Oregon, 'US-OH:michigan' the Toledo area, 'US-WV:western-pennsylvania' West Virginia). Its periods run oldest first: from a period's 'from' until the next period's 'from', the area was part of that period's 'shetach', given by the id in data/shetachim.json of that head's shetach today (Levitin's Pacific Northwest is 'washington'). Before the first period the area was in no shetach, as far as is known. 'heads' is keyed by shetach id: its heads, oldest first, each {head, from, name (what the shetach was called then, where it differs)}; a shetach with one head since it began lists him from its start, with the sources on the area period that starts it. 'events' is keyed by shetach id: vaads, passings and the like, each {date, what, sources}. Dates are 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'; when only bounds are known, 'from' is null and 'fromBound' is {after, by}. 'how': owner (the owner's own statement, taken as fact; owner, Nov 8: "I'm telling you as a fact ... I just need to figure out when each one split off. Stop trying to verify my facts"), stated (a source states it), news (a report from the time), anniversary (counted back), range (only bounds). 'confidence', as in data/founding-years.json: high (a report from the time, or the shetach's own statement, and nothing against it), medium (one later source, a count back, or sources a year apart), low, range, open; none on 'owner' periods. 'sources': [{url, title, date (the source's own), quote (its words), via (where an earlier session found it), note}]. Research notes: work/shetach-history/README.md.

sources.title: Monthly Mitzvah: Tzedakah (Jewish Review)
sources.quote: On Jan. 15, 1984 (Rosh Chodesh Shevat), Rabbi Moshe Wilhelm and family arrived in Portland and founded Chabad of Oregon.

US-OR:oregon.note: 15 Jan 1984 was 11 Shevat 5744; Rosh Chodesh Shevat was 5 Jan, so the day is uncertain; January 1984 either way.

sources.title: Lubavitcher Center
sources.note: Philadelphia City Paper (COLlive, 28 Aug 2009): 'Philadelphia became one of the first major U.S. cities with an outpost when Rabbi Avrohom Shemtov began his mission here in 1961, out in the far Northeast on Castor Avenue, where he still resides.' (The Lubavitcher Center, NE Philadelphia; Shemtov also began Torah classes on campus in 1962.)

sources.title: Merkos - Chabad of Rhode Island / Chabad of Providence
sources.note: ChabadInfo: Rabbi Yehoshua and Mishla Laufer 'established the Providence-based Chabad Center of greater Rhode Island in 1979'. 360-362 Hope Street.

sources.title: Chabad Center for Jewish Life
sources.note: The News & Observer (CrownHeights.info, 12 Dec 2008): 'The first Chabad House in the Tar Heel state was started in 1980 by Rabbi Yossi Groner of Charlotte.' Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 29 March 2025): 'Chabad in Charlotte was founded by Mushka's grandparents, Rabbi Yossi and Mariashi Groner, in 1980'. Rabbi Groner's own account (JEM, interviewed 2013; Anash.org, 9 Oct 2025): head emissary to North and South Carolina 'since 1980'; other biographies: sent 'in the summer of 1980'.

US-SC:the-carolinas.note: The shetach is both states (the owner's data); Groner's first house was Charlotte (1980).

sources.title: Chabad Jewish Center of South Dakota
sources.note: JTA (in the St. Louis Jewish Light, 27 Dec 2016): 'Rabbi Mendel and Mussie Alperowitz and their children arrived on Dec. 24 in Sioux Falls, where they will open a Chabad center.' Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 16 2016. Now 4901 S Isabel Pl, Suite 200.

US-SD:upper-midwest.note: South Dakota's first Chabad center; the state is in the Upper Midwest shetach (the owner's data).

sources.title: Chabad Lubavitch of Tennessee
sources.note: Lubavitch.com (11 Sept 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'When Chabad of Memphis opened in 1994, it found a close-knit Jewish community of 10,000'. Rabbi Levi and Rivka Klein (therebbesimpact.com: 1994).

US-TN:tennessee.note: Nashville had a Chabad rav from 1949, Rabbi Zalman Posner, sent by the Frierdiker Rebbe to its shul; the shetach dates from Chabad of Memphis (1994).

sources.title: Chabad Lubavitch Center Regional Hdqts.
sources.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 March 2003 ('A 30th B-day for Chabad of the Lone Star State'): Chabad Lubavitch of Texas 'celebrated 30 years in the state' on 9 March 2003; 'in 1972, when Rabbi Shimon and Chiena Lazaroff ... came to Houston'. The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 section on Chabad's 50 years in Texas (ChabadInfo, 'Chabad's 50-year Lone Star Journey'): 'When the Lazaroffs first arrived in Houston on May 10, 1972'; construction of the center on Fondren Road (the first Chabad center built from the ground up) began in 1977 and it opened for the High Holy Days in 1978 (CrownHeights.info, Jan 2007, says the center was founded in 1976); before that, an apartment.

sources.title: Chabad Lubavitch of Utah
sources.note: The Zippels came to Salt Lake City in 1992 (the Rebbe's blessing 1 Mar 1992); most reports say July 1992 (others fall, or April); 25 years marked in 2018, 30 in 2022 (KSL).

sources.title: New Torah Honors Life of Virginia's First Emissary (CrownHeights.info)
sources.quote: Rabbi Yossel Kranz, executive director of Chabad of the Virginias, whose father founded the center in 1976 at the direction of the Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson, of righteous memory.
sources.note: also: Rabbi Yaakov Noach "Yankel" Kranz 'directed Chabad-Lubavitch activities in the state for 15 years'

sources.title: Chabad of Vermont
sources.note: Chabad.org (20 Dec 2018): 'In the winter of 1983' Rabbi Yitzchok and Zeesy Raskin were appointed by the Rebbe 'as the new Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries to Vermont'; one of their first acts was a menorah at City Hall. A Chabad article also says they opened the center in 1983, but the Brattleboro Reformer (2012) and Front Porch Forum say 1984. Rabbi Eliyahu and Draizy Junik, now its directors, came in 2014. Checked (Nov 7): its own site (https://www.chabadvt.org/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/447745/jewish/About-Chabad-of-Burlington.htm): 'Founded by Rabbi Yitzchok and Zeesy Raskin in 1984'; so appointed in the winter of 1983 and founded 1984 — the year taken is the center's own (was 1983), medium as the two are a year apart.

US-VT:vermont.note: Appointed by the Rebbe 'in the winter of 1983' (Chabad.org, 2018); in Vermont from 1984.

sources.title: After more than 50 years, Lubavitch leader is still on a mission (Wisconsin Jewish Chronicle)
sources.quote: Shmotkin brought the Chabad movement to Wisconsin back in October of 1968.

US-WI:wisconsin.note: Lubavitch of Wisconsin: 'In 1968 the Rebbe appointed Rabbi Yisroel and B. Devorah Shmotkin as the Shluchim to the state of Wisconsin' (chabadwi.org, as quoted by a search). The seventh Merkos regional office, by the JTA's count of January 1970 (Kansas City the eighth).

sources.title: Chabad may soon have a W.Va. house (Pittsburgh Jewish Chronicle, on CrownHeights.info)
sources.quote: Officially, Chabad activities in West Virginia are supervised by Chabad of Virginia. However, because Morgantown is so close to Pittsburgh, Rabbi Yisroel Rosenfeld of the Lubavitch Center is also assisting Gurevitz in establishing a Morgantown presence.

sources.title: New Arrivals Working to Strengthen Jewish Life in West Virginia (Chabad.org)
sources.quote: "I think there are a lot of people here who don't have many opportunities to do something Jewish," said Gurevitz, who, under the aegis of Chabad-Lubavitch of Virginia, co-directs West Virginia's first Chabad House.

sources.title: Morgantown Chabad to close on $1.2M purchase of house near WVU (Pittsburgh Jewish Chronicle)
sources.quote: Chabad of Morgantown falls under the auspices of the Lubavitch Center of Pittsburgh, under the direction of Rabbi Yisroel Rosenfeld. It was Rosenfeld who assigned the Gurevitzes to Morgantown six years ago.

US-WV:western-pennsylvania.note: West Virginia's first shliach, (Shneur) Zalman Gurevitz, opened in Morgantown in 2007 under Chabad of Virginia, with Rosenfeld helping; by Dec 2013 the house was under Pittsburgh. So the move came after the first shliach, not with him (the owner, Nov 8: "once West Virginia got a shliach under Rosenfeld, that changed the calculus").

US-WY:wyoming.note: Owner, Nov 8: "Yes, if his offices thing includes it, then it makes sense": Anash.org (Aug 4 2021): "Chabad of the Pacific North West covers British Colombia, Alberta, Alaska, Montana, Oregon, Wyoming and Washington".

sources.title: Chabad-Lubavitch of Wyoming
sources.note: 8 May 2008: 'Rabbi Zalman and Raizy Mendelsohn arrived in the mountainous state of Wyoming on Thursday' to open the state's first Chabad center (the Jackson Hole Star-Tribune gave May 6). In 2023 they had been Wyoming's only shluchim 'for the past 15 years'. (therebbesimpact.com's 2007 is wrong.)

florida.what: Rabbi Avrohom Korf's letter (dated Yud Shvat 5780) names a seven-member Vaad Hashluchim to represent him "in all aspects of Shlichus in the state of Florida" and says he will "defer all decisions to them and will accept their decisions as final"; in a follow-up email: "I would never give up my Shlichus". A vaad had been set up a few months before; this named its members.

sources.title: Florida Head Shliach Clarifies Abdicating His Role (COLlive)
New Vaad Appointed To Help Oversee Chabad Activities In Florida (CrownHeights.info)
sources.quote: Rabbi Korf notes that the Vaads decisions in matters of placement of new Shluchim, contracts between Shluchim, arbitration, and uniform codes will be final.

florida.what: Rabbi Avrohom Korf passed away (12 Tammuz 5785).
At the Florida kinus, at the shloshim, Merkos names his son Rabbi Bentzion (Benjy) Korf head shliach (heads.florida).

new-jersey.what: New Jersey's first vaad: one member 'was appointed to New Jersey's original Vaad 15 years ago' (June 2025), so about 2010.

sources.title: New Vaad Hashluchim Elected in New Jersey (Anash.org)

new-jersey.what: Rabbi Moshe Herson passed away (23 Teves 5785).
A new five-member Vaad Hashluchim is elected to serve alongside Rabbi Mendy Herson.

virginia.what: Rabbi Yaakov Noach (Yankel) Kranz passed away (6 Elul 5751); in Sept 2011 Richmond marked '20 years since the passing'.

southern-ohio.what: Kalmanson removed as head shliach (owner, Nov 8: "Kalmanson was kicked off the year after gimmel tammuz").
His organization kept the name: the JTA, on the Supreme Court's order allowing the menorah in Cincinnati's Fountain Square, calls him 'regional director of Chabad of Southern Ohio'.

sources.title: U.S. Supreme Court Intervenes to Allow Menorah in Cincinnati (JTA)
sources.note: as a search quotes it

northeast-ohio.what: Rabbi Leibel Alevsky passed away (3 Iyar 5786).
